checks.name: repository-control-scope-is-alive
checks.summary: the proof that the dead scope is alive, with both controls. Positive control (the assertion that fails on the starting tree): after registering a Repository, capturing a Requirement naming it and planning an Increment, the stored canonical target's RepositoryID is non-empty and equals the registered id. domain.ControlApplies holds for a domain.ScopeRepository intent naming that id. Negative control: the same intent with a different repository id does not match, and end to end through Service.Control the matching intent's ControlProgress carries exactly one target (the claimed lease, with the right RepositoryID) while the non-matching intent's ControlProgress carries none. internal/domain/control.go is unchanged: matching always worked, it had simply never been given a non-empty value to match.

checks.name: heartbeat-carries-no-repository
checks.summary: the recorded RunnerObservation's target has an empty RepositoryID, a domain.ScopeRepository intent naming a registered Repository does NOT match it, and the runner-scoped intent that is meant to reach it still does. This is a deliberate design choice, not an omission: HeartbeatRequest names a Runner and carries neither an Increment nor a Lease, and one Runner serves every Repository of the Installation, so attaching a repository would make a repository-scoped stop apply to unrelated work.

checks.name: snapshot-fallback-resolves-the-repository
checks.summary: two active leases are seeded directly (Plan is what stores a canonical target, so a lease with none cannot be produced by running Plan; this is the state a lease created before this change is in). Both increments are asserted to have no canonical target first, so the fallback really is the path under test. A repository-scoped intent then matches exactly the lease whose Requirement carries a link, with RepositoryID, IncrementID, RunnerID, LeaseID and ExecutionID all correct -- the fill-only-when-empty RunnerID merge is unchanged -- and does not match the unlinked one.

checks.name: capture-ceremony-and-refusals
checks.summary: Capture writes the link inside its existing transaction, following its own ceremony step for step (callerActor role check, requestedBy attribution, requireRequest, requestFingerprint, s.mutate keyed by operation and request id, the Idempotency replay/conflict read, a domain.Permit gate on domain.PermitIntake with a ControlTarget naming the supplied repository, and one s.record event). The link carries Capture's own requestedBy and an assignment instant from the injected clock. A Capture with no repository_id behaves exactly as before and writes no link. A Capture naming an unregistered Repository is refused as ErrNotFound and a Capture naming a retired Repository as ErrRepositoryNotAvailable, and in both cases no Requirement is created. Write-once is asserted in both directions: the identical link re-written is an idempotent replay that leaves the record unchanged, a second link naming a different Repository is refused with domain.ErrStaleVersion and does not alter the stored link.

checks.name: fourth-observable-is-measured
checks.summary: RepositoryBacklogView gained RequirementCount and Truncated, its State is ObservedMeasured when the count was actually read, and InstallationScope keeps its name and its Installation-wide meaning. TestRepositoryDetailRendersAllSixDeclaredObservables was updated IN PLACE -- same name, only the backlog assertion changed from ObservedUnobserved to the measured count, every other observable's assertion untouched, no second test added to shadow it. The new tests measure two Requirements on one Repository and one on another while the Installation-wide summary reports all four, and assert that a linked Requirement's row and detail carry repository_id while an unlinked one omits it. The row and backlog assertions are two separate tests because each bounded owner read reserves internal/quota.ReadTransactionUsage (6,001 reads) against the Installation's daily budget, which is a real production property: five reads on one store exhaust it.
